study_identification_part.si_4_title: Age-atypical brain functional networks in autism spectrum disorder: a normative modeling approach

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: Local polynomial regression (LOESS) used to fit age-related normative trajectories of FC.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: We used a method called the local polynomial regression fitting process (LOESS) to determine the local width or smoothing kernel of the regression model based on the minimum squared error model provided across the entire age range

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: Resting-state fMRI functional connectivity, summarized as within- and between-network FC (W-scores).
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: we analyzed individuals with ASD and typically developed (TD) controls (total n = 1218) aged 5 -40 years, generating individualized whole-brain network functional connectivity (FC) maps of age-related atypicality in ASD.; The ABIDE dataset is a large-scale open-access neuroimaging dataset for ASD, which currently includes resting-state fMRI data from 1495 individuals collected at 17 data acquisition centers.
nm2_2_response_variable.location: Jiang2024.pdf.md: Abstract; S0033291724000138sup001.docx.md: Online supplement 1 Dataset details

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: Age used as the clinical covariate to predict FC in the normative model.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: This enables prediction of the FC value (the dark contour line) from the clinical covariates (age) along with measures of predictive confidence (the two lighter contour lines).
